title: Final Versus Intermediate Parity Checks
summary: The authors believe a single final parity check offers the best performance-versus-fault-detection tradeoff, but the comparison with intermediate checks remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a code-abiding permutation protected by parity equations, faults injected at different computation steps may propagate in hard-to-predict ways and may compensate, producing an erroneous state that still decodes successfully; the unresolved task is to determine whether checking the parity equations only once at the end provides a better performance-versus-fault-detection tradeoff than adding intermediate checks between steps.

scope.domain: This concerns fault detection in parity-protected permutations for authenticated encryption.
parameters: Parity-check placement: compares a single check at the end with intermediate checks between computation steps
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether a single parity check at the end provides a better performance-versus-fault-detection tradeoff than intermediate parity checks.

citations.label: Friet: an Authenticated Encryption Scheme with Built-in Fault Detection

progress.summary: The source presents the authors' belief that intermediate parity checks are not worth their cost because faults can propagate unpredictably and compensate. It favors a single final check but does not resolve the comparison.
citation_labels: Thierry Simon et al., Friet: an Authenticated Encryption Scheme with Built-in Fault Detection
